registration.name: Marla Denny

answers.How are registration accounts opened, an: Registration opens the account at the desk. A returning patient gets a second account by mistake - misspelled search, busy night. Duplicate charts are the same person; merging them is routine, safe work.
answers.What pivot year does the system use for: The window starts at 1930. 30 and up is 19-something, under 30 is 20-something. A woman born in 1929 shows up as a small child.
answers.Tell me about the allergy field on the r: It is free text the registrar types on the account. NKA when the patient reports none. It occasionally says NKA and lists an allergy anyway, when an old chart is copied forward.
answers.Does the lab re-issue its account number: The lab re-issues its account numbers every year or so, the way the old card files were purged.

registration.outside_response: Outside my area. That is another department - ask them.

lab.name: Tom Reyes

answers.How are lab collection dates encoded?: Collection dates are Julian: a two-digit year and the day of the year. Day 100 of 2026 is April 10, 2026. The day-of-year field sits next to the year on the result record.
answers.What unit is potassium reported in?: MEQ/L. The range on the test dictionary, 3.5 to 5.1, is the giveaway.
answers.What happens to a lab result that is not: A result that is not a number is a bench error. The bench cleans those up; you do not convert them.
answers.Is the lab account number the patient's: The L number is the patient. An L number, once opened, is never reused or re-issued.

lab.outside_response: Outside my area. Ask the owning department.

answers.What are the misc-med orders, and can th: A misc-med order means the real order is written in the patient's notes, and pharmacy works from the note. They are real orders for real patients. You can leave the misc-med orders out of a conversion; the note holds the details anyway.
answers.When two charts look alike, are they the: Most charts that look like duplicates are different people - spouses, parents and children at one address. Merging on name and birth date alone is how a conversion hurts someone.

systems.name: Greg Holt

answers.What pivot year does the system use for: The pivot year of 50: 00-49 are 20xx, 50-99 are 19xx. I set it from the vendor release note.
answers.Is the data dictionary current?: The dictionary is current. I maintain it, and it describes the system the extract comes from.
answers.Does the hospital have a master patient: There is no master index and never was. Each department assigns its own account numbers; the vendor sells an index as a separate module the hospital did not buy.
answers.What does appointment status R mean?: R is not a status in the dictionary. The documented statuses are B, C, N, A, X.

systems.outside_response: Outside my area. The departments own that.
